A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FideDiff work, and their text, equations, figures, and tables support reliable comparison. Both end with references; neither includes an appendix or the separate supplementary material mentioned in the text.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original FideDiff benchmark results, inference timings, and ablations in Tables 2–7, alongside qualitative image comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and reports additional foundation-model ablation results in Table 4.

M1.justification: Trajectory consistency training, learnable text embeddings, EA-LPIPS and GAN losses, Kernel ControlNet, and timestep prediction already appear in v1. The revised multiplication notation clarifies the elementwise operation already depicted in v1 Figure 4; it does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use original and enlarged GoPro training data and evaluate GoPro, HIDE, RealBlur-J, and RealBlur-R. The added ablations use existing GoPro coverage without introducing another task or test scenario.

E2.justification: The reported benchmark comparators remain Restormer, HI-Diff, UFPNet, AdaRevD, DiffBIR, OSEDiff, Diff-Plugin, and UID-Diff. The existing comparisons in Tables 5 and 7 are also retained; the new Table 4 rows are internal component ablations.

E3.justification: Table 4 adds controls using ordinary LPIPS and fixed text embeddings at downsampling factor 8 and patch size 384. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged. Specifying original GoPro for the foundation ablation supplies additional detail rather than establishing a dataset switch.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds separate tests of edge enhancement in the perceptual loss and learnable versus fixed text embeddings. Existing discriminator, downsampling, patch-size, Kernel ControlNet, consistency-training, and timestep analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or variability estimates. The added ablation rows retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds ordinary LPIPS with a learnable embedding (PSNR 26.12, LPIPS 0.1119) and EA-LPIPS with a fixed embedding (26.07, 0.1138). The five matched earlier ablation rows, other numerical tables, and plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The diffusion and blur-process formulations, consistency objective, and loss equations are retained. v2 repeats the reconstruction formula already given in Equation 3 and clarifies operator notation without adding mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about single-step high-fidelity deblurring, consistency training, Kernel ControlNet, adaptive timestep prediction, and comparative performance.

C2.justification: The substantive interpretations concerning generalization, fidelity–perception trade-offs, VAE detail loss, memory constraints, and imperfect timestep prediction are retained. The added Table 4 commentary reports the new ablation findings without introducing a distinct limitation or explanatory argument.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly discloses omission of the tokenizer and text encoder, clarifies kernel-conditioning operations, and identifies Table 4's original-GoPro setting, embedding controls, and edge-enhanced loss labels. Hardware information and the promised code/data release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work adds Hu et al. (2023) on autonomous driving, Liu et al. (2025b) on interacted object grounding, and Liu et al. (2025a) on one-step motion deblurring. These modestly broaden positioning without changing the central novelty claims.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording edits and expands method and ablation explanations. It adds acknowledgements, ethics, and reproducibility statements while retaining the main section sequence and most prose.

P2.justification: Figure 4 gains intermediate-variable labels and clearer operation symbols. Table 4 expands from five to seven rows, adds an LE column, and reorganizes its settings. Conference headers and local page reflow accompany these limited display changes.

improvement.justification: Table 4 now separately tests embedding and edge-enhancement choices that v1 used without dedicated controls, while Section 4 and Figure 4 clarify implementation. These changes modestly strengthen experimental support and readability; the main method, benchmark results, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
